speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: If music be the food of love, play on. Give me excess of it, that, surfeiting, The appetite may sicken and so die. That strain again! It had a dying fall. O, it came o’er my ear like the sweet sound That breathes upon a bank of violets, Stealing and giving odor. Enough; no more. ’Tis not so sweet now as it was before. O spirit of love, how quick and fresh art thou, That, notwithstanding thy capacity Receiveth as the sea, naught enters there, Of what validity and pitch soe’er, But falls into abatement and low price Even in a minute. So full of shapes is fancy That it alone is high fantastical.

speeches.speaker: CURIO
speeches.text: Will you go hunt, my lord?

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: What, Curio?

speeches.speaker: CURIO
speeches.text: The hart.

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: Why, so I do, the noblest that I have. O, when mine eyes did see Olivia first, Methought she purged the air of pestilence. That instant was I turned into a hart, And my desires, like fell and cruel hounds, E’er since pursue me. How now, what news from her?

speeches.speaker: VALENTINE
speeches.text: So please my lord, I might not be admitted, But from her handmaid do return this answer: The element itself, till seven years’ heat, Shall not behold her face at ample view, But like a cloistress she will veilèd walk, And water once a day her chamber round With eye-offending brine—all this to season A brother’s dead love, which she would keep fresh And lasting in her sad remembrance.

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: O, she that hath a heart of that fine frame To pay this debt of love but to a brother, How will she love when the rich golden shaft Hath killed the flock of all affections else That live in her; when liver, brain, and heart, These sovereign thrones, are all supplied, and filled Her sweet perfections with one self king! Away before me to sweet beds of flowers! Love thoughts lie rich when canopied with bowers.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: What country, friends, is this?

speeches.speaker: CAPTAIN
speeches.text: This is Illyria, lady.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: And what should I do in Illyria? My brother he is in Elysium. Perchance he is not drowned.—What think you, sailors?

speeches.speaker: CAPTAIN
speeches.text: It is perchance that you yourself were saved.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: O, my poor brother! And so perchance may he be.

speeches.speaker: CAPTAIN
speeches.text: True, madam. And to comfort you with chance, Assure yourself, after our ship did split, When you and those poor number saved with you Hung on our driving boat, I saw your brother, Most provident in peril, bind himself (Courage and hope both teaching him the practice) To a strong mast that lived upon the sea, Where, like Arion on the dolphin’s back, I saw him hold acquaintance with the waves So long as I could see.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: For saying so, there’s gold. Mine own escape unfoldeth to my hope, Whereto thy speech serves for authority, The like of him. Know’st thou this country?

speeches.speaker: CAPTAIN
speeches.text: Ay, madam, well, for I was bred and born Not three hours’ travel from this very place.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: Who governs here?

speeches.speaker: CAPTAIN
speeches.text: A noble duke, in nature as in name.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: What is his name?

speeches.speaker: CAPTAIN
speeches.text: Orsino.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: Orsino. I have heard my father name him. He was a bachelor then.

speeches.speaker: CAPTAIN
speeches.text: And so is now, or was so very late; For but a month ago I went from hence, And then ’twas fresh in murmur (as, you know, What great ones do the less will prattle of) That he did seek the love of fair Olivia.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: What’s she?

speeches.speaker: CAPTAIN
speeches.text: A virtuous maid, the daughter of a count That died some twelvemonth since, then leaving her In the protection of his son, her brother, Who shortly also died, for whose dear love, They say, she hath abjured the sight And company of men.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: O, that I served that lady, And might not be delivered to the world Till I had made mine own occasion mellow, What my estate is.

speeches.speaker: CAPTAIN
speeches.text: That were hard to compass Because she will admit no kind of suit, No, not the Duke’s.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: There is a fair behavior in thee, captain, And though that nature with a beauteous wall Doth oft close in pollution, yet of thee I will believe thou hast a mind that suits With this thy fair and outward character. I prithee—and I’ll pay thee bounteously— Conceal me what I am, and be my aid For such disguise as haply shall become The form of my intent. I’ll serve this duke. Thou shalt present me as an eunuch to him. It may be worth thy pains, for I can sing And speak to him in many sorts of music That will allow me very worth his service. What else may hap, to time I will commit. Only shape thou thy silence to my wit.

speeches.speaker: CAPTAIN
speeches.text: Be you his eunuch, and your mute I’ll be. When my tongue blabs, then let mine eyes not see.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: I thank thee. Lead me on.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: What a plague means my niece to take the death of her brother thus? I am sure care’s an enemy to life.

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: By my troth, Sir Toby, you must come in earlier o’ nights. Your cousin, my lady, takes great exceptions to your ill hours.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Why, let her except before excepted!

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: Ay, but you must confine yourself within the modest limits of order.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Confine? I’ll confine myself no finer than I am. These clothes are good enough to drink in, and so be these boots too. An they be not, let them hang themselves in their own straps!

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: That quaffing and drinking will undo you. I heard my lady talk of it yesterday, and of a foolish knight that you brought in one night here to be her wooer.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Who, Sir Andrew Aguecheek?

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: Ay, he.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: He’s as tall a man as any ’s in Illyria.

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: What’s that to th’ purpose?

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Why, he has three thousand ducats a year!

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: Ay, but he’ll have but a year in all these ducats. He’s a very fool and a prodigal.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Fie that you’ll say so! He plays o’ th’ viol-de-gamboys and speaks three or four languages word for word without book, and hath all the good gifts of nature.

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: He hath indeed, almost natural, for, besides that he’s a fool, he’s a great quarreler, and, but that he hath the gift of a coward to allay the gust he hath in quarreling, ’tis thought among the prudent he would quickly have the gift of a grave.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: By this hand, they are scoundrels and substractors that say so of him. Who are they?

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: They that add, moreover, he’s drunk nightly in your company.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: With drinking healths to my niece. I’ll drink to her as long as there is a passage in my throat and drink in Illyria. He’s a coward and a coistrel that will not drink to my niece till his brains turn o’ th’ toe like a parish top. What, wench! Castiliano vulgo, for here comes Sir Andrew Agueface.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: Sir Toby Belch! How now, Sir Toby Belch?

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Sweet Sir Andrew!

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: Bless you, fair shrew.

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: And you too, sir.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Accost, Sir Andrew, accost!

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: What’s that?

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: My niece’s chambermaid.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: Good Mistress Accost, I desire better acquaintance.

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: My name is Mary, sir.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: Good Mistress Mary Accost—

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: You mistake, knight. “Accost” is front her, board her, woo her, assail her.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: By my troth, I would not undertake her in this company. Is that the meaning of “accost”?

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: Fare you well, gentlemen.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: An thou let part so, Sir Andrew, would thou mightst never draw sword again.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: An you part so, mistress, I would I might never draw sword again. Fair lady, do you think you have fools in hand?

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: Sir, I have not you by th’ hand.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: Marry, but you shall have, and here’s my hand.

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: Now sir, thought is free. I pray you, bring your hand to th’ butt’ry bar and let it drink.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: Wherefore, sweetheart? What’s your metaphor?

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: It’s dry, sir.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: Why, I think so. I am not such an ass but I can keep my hand dry. But what’s your jest?

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: A dry jest, sir.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: Are you full of them?

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: Ay, sir, I have them at my fingers’ ends. Marry, now I let go your hand, I am barren.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: O knight, thou lack’st a cup of canary! When did I see thee so put down?

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: Never in your life, I think, unless you see canary put me down. Methinks sometimes I have no more wit than a Christian or an ordinary man has. But I am a great eater of beef, and I believe that does harm to my wit.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: No question.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: An I thought that, I’d forswear it. I’ll ride home tomorrow, Sir Toby.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Pourquoi, my dear knight?

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: What is “pourquoi”? Do, or not do? I would I had bestowed that time in the tongues that I have in fencing, dancing, and bearbaiting. O, had I but followed the arts!

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Then hadst thou had an excellent head of hair.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: Why, would that have mended my hair?

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Past question, for thou seest it will not curl by nature.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: But it becomes me well enough, does ’t not?

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Excellent! It hangs like flax on a distaff, and I hope to see a huswife take thee between her legs and spin it off.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: Faith, I’ll home tomorrow, Sir Toby. Your niece will not be seen, or if she be, it’s four to one she’ll none of me. The Count himself here hard by woos her.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: She’ll none o’ th’ Count. She’ll not match above her degree, neither in estate, years, nor wit. I have heard her swear ’t. Tut, there’s life in ’t, man.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: I’ll stay a month longer. I am a fellow o’ th’ strangest mind i’ th’ world. I delight in masques and revels sometimes altogether.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Art thou good at these kickshawses, knight?

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: As any man in Illyria, whatsoever he be, under the degree of my betters, and yet I will not compare with an old man.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: What is thy excellence in a galliard, knight?

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: Faith, I can cut a caper.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: And I can cut the mutton to ’t.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: And I think I have the back-trick simply as strong as any man in Illyria.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Wherefore are these things hid? Wherefore have these gifts a curtain before ’em? Are they like to take dust, like Mistress Mall’s picture? Why dost thou not go to church in a galliard and come home in a coranto? My very walk should be a jig. I would not so much as make water but in a sink-a-pace. What dost thou mean? Is it a world to hide virtues in? I did think, by the excellent constitution of thy leg, it was formed under the star of a galliard.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: Ay, ’tis strong, and it does indifferent well in a dun-colored stock. Shall we set about some revels?

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: What shall we do else? Were we not born under Taurus?

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: Taurus? That’s sides and heart.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: No, sir, it is legs and thighs. Let me see thee caper. Ha, higher! Ha, ha, excellent!

speeches.speaker: VALENTINE
speeches.text: If the Duke continue these favors towards you, Cesario, you are like to be much advanced. He hath known you but three days, and already you are no stranger.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: You either fear his humor or my negligence, that you call in question the continuance of his love. Is he inconstant, sir, in his favors?

speeches.speaker: VALENTINE
speeches.text: No, believe me.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: I thank you. Here comes the Count.

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: Who saw Cesario, ho?

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: On your attendance, my lord, here.

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: Stand you awhile aloof.—Cesario, Thou know’st no less but all. I have unclasped To thee the book even of my secret soul. Therefore, good youth, address thy gait unto her. Be not denied access. Stand at her doors And tell them, there thy fixèd foot shall grow Till thou have audience.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: Sure, my noble lord, If she be so abandoned to her sorrow As it is spoke, she never will admit me.

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: Be clamorous and leap all civil bounds Rather than make unprofited return.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: Say I do speak with her, my lord, what then?

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: O, then unfold the passion of my love. Surprise her with discourse of my dear faith. It shall become thee well to act my woes. She will attend it better in thy youth Than in a nuncio’s of more grave aspect.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: I think not so, my lord.

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: Dear lad, believe it; For they shall yet belie thy happy years That say thou art a man. Diana’s lip Is not more smooth and rubious, thy small pipe Is as the maiden’s organ, shrill and sound, And all is semblative a womans part. I know thy constellation is right apt For this affair.—Some four or five attend him, All, if you will, for I myself am best When least in company.—Prosper well in this And thou shalt live as freely as thy lord, To call his fortunes thine.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: I’ll do my best To woo your lady. Yet a barful strife! Whoe’er I woo, myself would be his wife.

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: Nay, either tell me where thou hast been, or I will not open my lips so wide as a bristle may enter in way of thy excuse. My lady will hang thee for thy absence.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Let her hang me. He that is well hanged in this world needs to fear no colors.

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: Make that good.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: He shall see none to fear.

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: A good Lenten answer. I can tell thee where that saying was born, of “I fear no colors.”

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Where, good Mistress Mary?

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: In the wars; and that may you be bold to say in your foolery.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Well, God give them wisdom that have it, and those that are Fools, let them use their talents.

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: Yet you will be hanged for being so long absent. Or to be turned away, is not that as good as a hanging to you?

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Many a good hanging prevents a bad marriage, and, for turning away, let summer bear it out.

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: You are resolute, then?

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Not so, neither, but I am resolved on two points.

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: That if one break, the other will hold, or if both break, your gaskins fall.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Apt, in good faith, very apt. Well, go thy way. If Sir Toby would leave drinking, thou wert as witty a piece of Eve’s flesh as any in Illyria.

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: Peace, you rogue. No more o’ that. Here comes my lady. Make your excuse wisely, you were best.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Wit, an ’t be thy will, put me into good fooling! Those wits that think they have thee do very oft prove fools, and I that am sure I lack thee may pass for a wise man. For what says Quinapalus? “Better a witty Fool than a foolish wit.”—God bless thee, lady!

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Take the Fool away.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Do you not hear, fellows? Take away the Lady.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Go to, you’re a dry Fool. I’ll no more of you. Besides, you grow dishonest.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Two faults, madonna, that drink and good counsel will amend. For give the dry Fool drink, then is the Fool not dry. Bid the dishonest man mend himself; if he mend, he is no longer dishonest; if he cannot, let the botcher mend him. Anything that’s mended is but patched; virtue that transgresses is but patched with sin, and sin that amends is but patched with virtue. If that this simple syllogism will serve, so; if it will not, what remedy? As there is no true cuckold but calamity, so beauty’s a flower. The Lady bade take away the Fool. Therefore, I say again, take her away.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Sir, I bade them take away you.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Misprision in the highest degree! Lady, cucullus non facit monachum. That’s as much to say as, I wear not motley in my brain. Good madonna, give me leave to prove you a fool.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Can you do it?

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Dexteriously, good madonna.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Make your proof.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: I must catechize you for it, madonna. Good my mouse of virtue, answer me.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Well, sir, for want of other idleness, I’ll bide your proof.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Good madonna, why mourn’st thou?

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Good Fool, for my brother’s death.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: I think his soul is in hell, madonna.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: I know his soul is in heaven, Fool.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: The more fool, madonna, to mourn for your brother’s soul, being in heaven. Take away the fool, gentlemen.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: What think you of this Fool, Malvolio? Doth he not mend?

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: Yes, and shall do till the pangs of death shake him. Infirmity, that decays the wise, doth ever make the better Fool.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: God send you, sir, a speedy infirmity, for the better increasing your folly! Sir Toby will be sworn that I am no fox, but he will not pass his word for twopence that you are no fool.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: How say you to that, Malvolio?

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: I marvel your Ladyship takes delight in such a barren rascal. I saw him put down the other day with an ordinary fool that has no more brain than a stone. Look you now, he’s out of his guard already. Unless you laugh and minister occasion to him, he is gagged. I protest I take these wise men that crow so at these set kind of Fools no better than the Fools’ zanies.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: O, you are sick of self-love, Malvolio, and taste with a distempered appetite. To be generous, guiltless, and of free disposition is to take those things for bird-bolts that you deem cannon bullets. There is no slander in an allowed Fool, though he do nothing but rail; nor no railing in a known discreet man, though he do nothing but reprove.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Now Mercury endue thee with leasing, for thou speak’st well of Fools!

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: Madam, there is at the gate a young gentleman much desires to speak with you.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: From the Count Orsino, is it?

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: I know not, madam. ’Tis a fair young man, and well attended.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Who of my people hold him in delay?

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: Sir Toby, madam, your kinsman.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Fetch him off, I pray you. He speaks nothing but madman. Fie on him! Go you, Malvolio. If it be a suit from the Count, I am sick, or not at home; what you will, to dismiss it. Now you see, sir, how your fooling grows old, and people dislike it.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Thou hast spoke for us, madonna, as if thy eldest son should be a Fool, whose skull Jove cram with brains, for—here he comes—one of thy kin has a most weak pia mater.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: By mine honor, half drunk!—What is he at the gate, cousin?

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: A gentleman.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: A gentleman? What gentleman?

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: ’Tis a gentleman here—a plague o’ these pickle herring!—How now, sot?

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Good Sir Toby.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Cousin, cousin, how have you come so early by this lethargy?

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Lechery? I defy lechery. There’s one at the gate.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Ay, marry, what is he?

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Let him be the devil an he will, I care not. Give me faith, say I. Well, it’s all one.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: What’s a drunken man like, Fool?

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Like a drowned man, a fool, and a madman. One draught above heat makes him a fool, the second mads him, and a third drowns him.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Go thou and seek the crowner and let him sit o’ my coz, for he’s in the third degree of drink: he’s drowned. Go look after him.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: He is but mad yet, madonna, and the Fool shall look to the madman.

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: Madam, yond young fellow swears he will speak with you. I told him you were sick; he takes on him to understand so much, and therefore comes to speak with you. I told him you were asleep; he seems to have a foreknowledge of that too, and therefore comes to speak with you. What is to be said to him, lady? He’s fortified against any denial.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Tell him he shall not speak with me.

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: Has been told so, and he says he’ll stand at your door like a sheriff’s post and be the supporter to a bench, but he’ll speak with you.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: What kind o’ man is he?

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: Why, of mankind.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: What manner of man?

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: Of very ill manner. He’ll speak with you, will you or no.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Of what personage and years is he?

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: Not yet old enough for a man, nor young enough for a boy—as a squash is before ’tis a peascod, or a codling when ’tis almost an apple. ’Tis with him in standing water, between boy and man. He is very well-favored, and he speaks very shrewishly. One would think his mother’s milk were scarce out of him.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Let him approach. Call in my gentlewoman.

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: Gentlewoman, my lady calls.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Give me my veil. Come, throw it o’er my face. We’ll once more hear Orsino’s embassy.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: The honorable lady of the house, which is she?

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Speak to me. I shall answer for her. Your will?

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: Most radiant, exquisite, and unmatchable beauty—I pray you, tell me if this be the lady of the house, for I never saw her. I would be loath to cast away my speech, for, besides that it is excellently well penned, I have taken great pains to con it. Good beauties, let me sustain no scorn. I am very comptible even to the least sinister usage.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Whence came you, sir?

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: I can say little more than I have studied, and that question’s out of my part. Good gentle one, give me modest assurance if you be the lady of the house, that I may proceed in my speech.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Are you a comedian?

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: No, my profound heart. And yet by the very fangs of malice I swear I am not that I play. Are you the lady of the house?

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: If I do not usurp myself, I am.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: Most certain, if you are she, you do usurp yourself, for what is yours to bestow is not yours to reserve. But this is from my commission. I will on with my speech in your praise and then show you the heart of my message.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Come to what is important in ’t. I forgive you the praise.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: Alas, I took great pains to study it, and ’tis poetical.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: It is the more like to be feigned. I pray you, keep it in. I heard you were saucy at my gates, and allowed your approach rather to wonder at you than to hear you. If you be not mad, begone; if you have reason, be brief. ’Tis not that time of moon with me to make one in so skipping a dialogue.

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: Will you hoist sail, sir? Here lies your way.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: No, good swabber, I am to hull here a little longer.—Some mollification for your giant, sweet lady.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Tell me your mind.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: I am a messenger.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Sure you have some hideous matter to deliver when the courtesy of it is so fearful. Speak your office.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: It alone concerns your ear. I bring no overture of war, no taxation of homage. I hold the olive in my hand. My words are as full of peace as matter.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Yet you began rudely. What are you? What would you?

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: The rudeness that hath appeared in me have I learned from my entertainment. What I am and what I would are as secret as maidenhead: to your ears, divinity; to any other’s, profanation.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Give us the place alone. We will hear this divinity. Now, sir, what is your text?

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: Most sweet lady—

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: A comfortable doctrine, and much may be said of it. Where lies your text?

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: In Orsino’s bosom.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: In his bosom? In what chapter of his bosom?

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: To answer by the method, in the first of his heart.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: O, I have read it; it is heresy. Have you no more to say?

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: Good madam, let me see your face.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Have you any commission from your lord to negotiate with my face? You are now out of your text. But we will draw the curtain and show you the picture. Look you, sir, such a one I was this present. Is ’t not well done?

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: Excellently done, if God did all.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: ’Tis in grain, sir; ’twill endure wind and weather.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: ’Tis beauty truly blent, whose red and white Nature’s own sweet and cunning hand laid on. Lady, you are the cruel’st she alive If you will lead these graces to the grave And leave the world no copy.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: O, sir, I will not be so hard-hearted! I will give out divers schedules of my beauty. It shall be inventoried and every particle and utensil labeled to my will: as, item, two lips indifferent red; item, two gray eyes with lids to them; item, one neck, one chin, and so forth. Were you sent hither to praise me?

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: I see you what you are. You are too proud. But if you were the devil you are fair. My lord and master loves you. O, such love Could be but recompensed though you were crowned The nonpareil of beauty.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: How does he love me?

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: With adorations, fertile tears, With groans that thunder love, with sighs of fire.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Your lord does know my mind. I cannot love him. Yet I suppose him virtuous, know him noble, Of great estate, of fresh and stainless youth; In voices well divulged, free, learned, and valiant, And in dimension and the shape of nature A gracious person. But yet I cannot love him. He might have took his answer long ago.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: If I did love you in my master’s flame, With such a suff’ring, such a deadly life, In your denial I would find no sense. I would not understand it.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Why, what would you?

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: Make me a willow cabin at your gate And call upon my soul within the house, Write loyal cantons of contemnèd love And sing them loud even in the dead of night, Hallow your name to the reverberate hills And make the babbling gossip of the air Cry out “Olivia!” O, you should not rest Between the elements of air and earth But you should pity me.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: You might do much. What is your parentage?

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: Above my fortunes, yet my state is well. I am a gentleman.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Get you to your lord. I cannot love him. Let him send no more— Unless perchance you come to me again To tell me how he takes it. Fare you well. I thank you for your pains. Spend this for me.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: I am no fee’d post, lady. Keep your purse. My master, not myself, lacks recompense. Love make his heart of flint that you shall love, And let your fervor, like my master’s, be Placed in contempt. Farewell, fair cruelty.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: “What is your parentage?” “Above my fortunes, yet my state is well. I am a gentleman.” I’ll be sworn thou art. Thy tongue, thy face, thy limbs, actions, and spirit Do give thee fivefold blazon. Not too fast! Soft, soft! Unless the master were the man. How now? Even so quickly may one catch the plague? Methinks I feel this youth’s perfections With an invisible and subtle stealth To creep in at mine eyes. Well, let it be.— What ho, Malvolio!

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: Here, madam, at your service.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Run after that same peevish messenger, The County’s man. He left this ring behind him, Would I or not. Tell him I’ll none of it. Desire him not to flatter with his lord, Nor hold him up with hopes. I am not for him. If that the youth will come this way tomorrow, I’ll give him reasons for ’t. Hie thee, Malvolio.

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: Madam, I will.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: I do I know not what, and fear to find Mine eye too great a flatterer for my mind. Fate, show thy force. Ourselves we do not owe. What is decreed must be, and be this so.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Will you stay no longer? Nor will you not that I go with you?

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
speeches.text: By your patience, no. My stars shine darkly over me. The malignancy of my fate might perhaps distemper yours. Therefore I shall crave of you your leave that I may bear my evils alone. It were a bad recompense for your love to lay any of them on you.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Let me yet know of you whither you are bound.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
speeches.text: No, sooth, sir. My determinate voyage is mere extravagancy. But I perceive in you so excellent a touch of modesty that you will not extort from me what I am willing to keep in. Therefore it charges me in manners the rather to express myself. You must know of me, then, Antonio, my name is Sebastian, which I called Roderigo. My father was that Sebastian of Messaline whom I know you have heard of. He left behind him myself and a sister, both born in an hour. If the heavens had been pleased, would we had so ended! But you, sir, altered that, for some hour before you took me from the breach of the sea was my sister drowned.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Alas the day!

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
speeches.text: A lady, sir, though it was said she much resembled me, was yet of many accounted beautiful. But though I could not with such estimable wonder overfar believe that, yet thus far I will boldly publish her: she bore a mind that envy could not but call fair. She is drowned already, sir, with salt water, though I seem to drown her remembrance again with more.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Pardon me, sir, your bad entertainment.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
speeches.text: O good Antonio, forgive me your trouble.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: If you will not murder me for my love, let me be your servant.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
speeches.text: If you will not undo what you have done— that is, kill him whom you have recovered—desire it not. Fare you well at once. My bosom is full of kindness, and I am yet so near the manners of my mother that, upon the least occasion more, mine eyes will tell tales of me. I am bound to the Count Orsino’s court. Farewell.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: The gentleness of all the gods go with thee! I have many enemies in Orsino’s court, Else would I very shortly see thee there. But come what may, I do adore thee so That danger shall seem sport, and I will go.

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: Were not you even now with the Countess Olivia?

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: Even now, sir. On a moderate pace I have since arrived but hither.

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: She returns this ring to you, sir. You might have saved me my pains to have taken it away yourself. She adds, moreover, that you should put your lord into a desperate assurance she will none of him. And one thing more, that you be never so hardy to come again in his affairs unless it be to report your lord’s taking of this. Receive it so.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: She took the ring of me. I’ll none of it.

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: Come, sir, you peevishly threw it to her, and her will is it should be so returned. If it be worth stooping for, there it lies in your eye; if not, be it his that finds it.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: I left no ring with her. What means this lady? Fortune forbid my outside have not charmed her! She made good view of me, indeed so much That methought her eyes had lost her tongue, For she did speak in starts distractedly. She loves me, sure! The cunning of her passion Invites me in this churlish messenger. None of my lord’s ring? Why, he sent her none! I am the man. If it be so, as ’tis, Poor lady, she were better love a dream. Disguise, I see thou art a wickedness Wherein the pregnant enemy does much. How easy is it for the proper false In women’s waxen hearts to set their forms! Alas, our frailty is the cause, not we, For such as we are made of, such we be. How will this fadge? My master loves her dearly, And I, poor monster, fond as much on him, And she, mistaken, seems to dote on me. What will become of this? As I am man, My state is desperate for my master’s love. As I am woman (now, alas the day!), What thriftless sighs shall poor Olivia breathe! O Time, thou must untangle this, not I. It is too hard a knot for me t’ untie.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Approach, Sir Andrew. Not to be abed after midnight is to be up betimes, and “diluculo surgere,” thou know’st—

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: Nay, by my troth, I know not. But I know to be up late is to be up late.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: A false conclusion. I hate it as an unfilled can. To be up after midnight and to go to bed then, is early, so that to go to bed after midnight is to go to bed betimes. Does not our lives consist of the four elements?

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: Faith, so they say, but I think it rather consists of eating and drinking.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Thou ’rt a scholar. Let us therefore eat and drink. Marian, I say, a stoup of wine!

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: Here comes the Fool, i’ faith.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: How now, my hearts? Did you never see the picture of We Three?

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Welcome, ass! Now let’s have a catch.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: By my troth, the Fool has an excellent breast. I had rather than forty shillings I had such a leg, and so sweet a breath to sing, as the Fool has.—In sooth, thou wast in very gracious fooling last night when thou spok’st of Pigrogromitus of the Vapians passing the equinoctial of Queubus. ’Twas very good, i’ faith. I sent thee sixpence for thy leman. Hadst it?

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: I did impeticos thy gratillity, for Malvolio’s nose is no whipstock, my lady has a white hand, and the Myrmidons are no bottle-ale houses.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: Excellent! Why, this is the best fooling when all is done. Now, a song!

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Come on, there is sixpence for you. Let’s have a song.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: There’s a testril of me, too. If one knight give a—

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Would you have a love song or a song of good life?

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: A love song, a love song.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: Ay, ay, I care not for good life.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: O mistress mine, where are you roaming? O, stay and hear! Your truelove’s coming, That can sing both high and low. Trip no further, pretty sweeting. Journeys end in lovers meeting, Every wise man’s son doth know.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: Excellent good, i’ faith!

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Good, good.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: What is love? ’Tis not hereafter. Present mirth hath present laughter. What’s to come is still unsure. In delay there lies no plenty, Then come kiss me, sweet and twenty. Youth’s a stuff will not endure.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: A mellifluous voice, as I am true knight.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: A contagious breath.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: Very sweet and contagious, i’ faith.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: To hear by the nose, it is dulcet in contagion. But shall we make the welkin dance indeed? Shall we rouse the night owl in a catch that will draw three souls out of one weaver? Shall we do that?

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: An you love me, let’s do ’t. I am dog at a catch.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: By ’r Lady, sir, and some dogs will catch well.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: Most certain. Let our catch be “Thou Knave.”

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: “Hold thy peace, thou knave,” knight? I shall be constrained in ’t to call thee “knave,” knight.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: ’Tis not the first time I have constrained one to call me “knave.” Begin, Fool. It begins “Hold thy peace.”

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: I shall never begin if I hold my peace.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: Good, i’ faith. Come, begin.

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: What a caterwauling do you keep here! If my lady have not called up her steward Malvolio and bid him turn you out of doors, never trust me.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: My lady’s a Cataian, we are politicians, Malvolio’s a Peg-a-Ramsey, and Three merry men be we. Am not I consanguineous? Am I not of her blood? Tillyvally! “Lady”! There dwelt a man in Babylon, lady, lady.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Beshrew me, the knight’s in admirable fooling.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: Ay, he does well enough if he be disposed, and so do I, too. He does it with a better grace, but I do it more natural.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: O’ the twelfth day of December—

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: For the love o’ God, peace!

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: My masters, are you mad? Or what are you? Have you no wit, manners, nor honesty but to gabble like tinkers at this time of night? Do you make an ale-house of my lady’s house, that you squeak out your coziers’ catches without any mitigation or remorse of voice? Is there no respect of place, persons, nor time in you?

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: We did keep time, sir, in our catches. Sneck up!

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: Sir Toby, I must be round with you. My lady bade me tell you that, though she harbors you as her kinsman, she’s nothing allied to your disorders. If you can separate yourself and your misdemeanors, you are welcome to the house; if not, an it would please you to take leave of her, she is very willing to bid you farewell.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Farewell, dear heart, since I must needs be gone.

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: Nay, good Sir Toby.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: His eyes do show his days are almost done.

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: Is ’t even so?

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: But I will never die.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Sir Toby, there you lie.

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: This is much credit to you.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Shall I bid him go?

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: What an if you do?

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Shall I bid him go, and spare not?

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: O no, no, no, no, you dare not.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Out o’ tune, sir? You lie. Art any more than a steward? Dost thou think, because thou art virtuous, there shall be no more cakes and ale?

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Yes, by Saint Anne, and ginger shall be hot i’ th’ mouth, too.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Thou ’rt i’ th’ right.—Go, sir, rub your chain with crumbs.—A stoup of wine, Maria!

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: Mistress Mary, if you prized my lady’s favor at anything more than contempt, you would not give means for this uncivil rule. She shall know of it, by this hand.

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: Go shake your ears!

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: ’Twere as good a deed as to drink when a man’s a-hungry, to challenge him the field and then to break promise with him and make a fool of him.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Do ’t, knight. I’ll write thee a challenge. Or I’ll deliver thy indignation to him by word of mouth.

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: Sweet Sir Toby, be patient for tonight. Since the youth of the Count’s was today with my lady, she is much out of quiet. For Monsieur Malvolio, let me alone with him. If I do not gull him into a nayword and make him a common recreation, do not think I have wit enough to lie straight in my bed. I know I can do it.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Possess us, possess us, tell us something of him.

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: Marry, sir, sometimes he is a kind of puritan.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: O, if I thought that, I’d beat him like a dog!

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: What, for being a puritan? Thy exquisite reason, dear knight?

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: I have no exquisite reason for ’t, but I have reason good enough.

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: The devil a puritan that he is, or anything constantly but a time-pleaser; an affectioned ass that cons state without book and utters it by great swaths; the best persuaded of himself, so crammed, as he thinks, with excellencies, that it is his grounds of faith that all that look on him love him. And on that vice in him will my revenge find notable cause to work.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: What wilt thou do?

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: I will drop in his way some obscure epistles of love, wherein by the color of his beard, the shape of his leg, the manner of his gait, the expressure of his eye, forehead, and complexion, he shall find himself most feelingly personated. I can write very like my lady your niece; on a forgotten matter, we can hardly make distinction of our hands.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Excellent! I smell a device.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: I have ’t in my nose, too.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: He shall think, by the letters that thou wilt drop, that they come from my niece, and that she’s in love with him.

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: My purpose is indeed a horse of that color.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: And your horse now would make him an ass.

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: Ass, I doubt not.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: O, ’twill be admirable!

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: Sport royal, I warrant you. I know my physic will work with him. I will plant you two, and let the Fool make a third, where he shall find the letter. Observe his construction of it. For this night, to bed, and dream on the event. Farewell.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Good night, Penthesilea.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: Before me, she’s a good wench.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: She’s a beagle true bred, and one that adores me. What o’ that?

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: I was adored once, too.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Let’s to bed, knight. Thou hadst need send for more money.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: If I cannot recover your niece, I am a foul way out.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Send for money, knight. If thou hast her not i’ th’ end, call me “Cut.”

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: If I do not, never trust me, take it how you will.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Come, come, I’ll go burn some sack. ’Tis too late to go to bed now. Come, knight; come, knight.

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: Give me some music. Now, good morrow, friends.— Now, good Cesario, but that piece of song, That old and antique song we heard last night. Methought it did relieve my passion much, More than light airs and recollected terms Of these most brisk and giddy-pacèd times. Come, but one verse.

speeches.speaker: CURIO
speeches.text: He is not here, so please your Lordship, that should sing it.

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: Who was it?

speeches.speaker: CURIO
speeches.text: Feste the jester, my lord, a Fool that the Lady Olivia’s father took much delight in. He is about the house.

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: Seek him out and play the tune the while. Come hither, boy. If ever thou shalt love, In the sweet pangs of it remember me, For such as I am, all true lovers are, Unstaid and skittish in all motions else Save in the constant image of the creature That is beloved. How dost thou like this tune?

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: It gives a very echo to the seat Where love is throned.

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: Thou dost speak masterly. My life upon ’t, young though thou art, thine eye Hath stayed upon some favor that it loves. Hath it not, boy?

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: A little, by your favor.

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: What kind of woman is ’t?

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: Of your complexion.

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: She is not worth thee, then. What years, i’ faith?

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: About your years, my lord.

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: Too old, by heaven. Let still the woman take An elder than herself. So wears she to him; So sways she level in her husband’s heart. For, boy, however we do praise ourselves, Our fancies are more giddy and unfirm, More longing, wavering, sooner lost and worn, Than women’s are.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: I think it well, my lord.

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: Then let thy love be younger than thyself, Or thy affection cannot hold the bent. For women are as roses, whose fair flower, Being once displayed, doth fall that very hour.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: And so they are. Alas, that they are so, To die even when they to perfection grow!

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: O, fellow, come, the song we had last night.— Mark it, Cesario. It is old and plain; The spinsters and the knitters in the sun And the free maids that weave their thread with bones Do use to chant it. It is silly sooth, And dallies with the innocence of love Like the old age.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Are you ready, sir?

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: Ay, prithee, sing.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Come away, come away, death, And in sad cypress let me be laid. Fly away, fly away, breath, I am slain by a fair cruel maid. My shroud of white, stuck all with yew, O, prepare it! My part of death, no one so true Did share it. Not a flower, not a flower sweet On my black coffin let there be strown; Not a friend, not a friend greet My poor corpse where my bones shall be thrown. A thousand thousand sighs to save, Lay me, O, where Sad true lover never find my grave To weep there.

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: There’s for thy pains.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: No pains, sir. I take pleasure in singing, sir.

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: I’ll pay thy pleasure, then.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Truly sir, and pleasure will be paid, one time or another.

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: Give me now leave to leave thee.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Now the melancholy god protect thee and the tailor make thy doublet of changeable taffeta, for thy mind is a very opal. I would have men of such constancy put to sea, that their business might be everything and their intent everywhere, for that’s it that always makes a good voyage of nothing. Farewell.

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: Let all the rest give place. Once more, Cesario, Get thee to yond same sovereign cruelty. Tell her my love, more noble than the world, Prizes not quantity of dirty lands. The parts that Fortune hath bestowed upon her, Tell her, I hold as giddily as Fortune. But ’tis that miracle and queen of gems That nature pranks her in attracts my soul.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: But if she cannot love you, sir—

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: I cannot be so answered.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: Sooth, but you must. Say that some lady, as perhaps there is, Hath for your love as great a pang of heart As you have for Olivia. You cannot love her; You tell her so. Must she not then be answered?

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: There is no woman’s sides Can bide the beating of so strong a passion As love doth give my heart; no woman’s heart So big, to hold so much; they lack retention. Alas, their love may be called appetite, No motion of the liver but the palate, That suffer surfeit, cloyment, and revolt; But mine is all as hungry as the sea, And can digest as much. Make no compare Between that love a woman can bear me And that I owe Olivia.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: Ay, but I know—

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: What dost thou know?

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: Too well what love women to men may owe. In faith, they are as true of heart as we. My father had a daughter loved a man As it might be, perhaps, were I a woman, I should your Lordship.

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: And what’s her history?

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: A blank, my lord. She never told her love, But let concealment, like a worm i’ th’ bud, Feed on her damask cheek. She pined in thought, And with a green and yellow melancholy She sat like Patience on a monument, Smiling at grief. Was not this love indeed? We men may say more, swear more, but indeed Our shows are more than will; for still we prove Much in our vows but little in our love.

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: But died thy sister of her love, my boy?

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: I am all the daughters of my father’s house, And all the brothers, too—and yet I know not. Sir, shall I to this lady?

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: Ay, that’s the theme. To her in haste. Give her this jewel. Say My love can give no place, bide no denay.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Come thy ways, Signior Fabian.

speeches.speaker: FABIAN
speeches.text: Nay, I’ll come. If I lose a scruple of this sport, let me be boiled to death with melancholy.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Wouldst thou not be glad to have the niggardly rascally sheep-biter come by some notable shame?

speeches.speaker: FABIAN
speeches.text: I would exult, man. You know he brought me out o’ favor with my lady about a bearbaiting here.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: To anger him, we’ll have the bear again, and we will fool him black and blue, shall we not, Sir Andrew?

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: An we do not, it is pity of our lives.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Here comes the little villain.—How now, my metal of India?

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: Get you all three into the boxtree. Malvolio’s coming down this walk. He has been yonder i’ the sun practicing behavior to his own shadow this half hour. Observe him, for the love of mockery, for I know this letter will make a contemplative idiot of him. Close, in the name of jesting! Lie thou there for here comes the trout that must be caught with tickling.

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: ’Tis but fortune, all is fortune. Maria once told me she did affect me, and I have heard herself come thus near, that should she fancy, it should be one of my complexion. Besides, she uses me with a more exalted respect than anyone else that follows her. What should I think on ’t?

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Here’s an overweening rogue.

speeches.speaker: FABIAN
speeches.text: O, peace! Contemplation makes a rare turkeycock of him. How he jets under his advanced plumes!

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: ’Slight, I could so beat the rogue!

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Peace, I say.

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: To be Count Malvolio.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Ah, rogue!

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: Pistol him, pistol him!

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Peace, peace!

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: There is example for ’t. The lady of the Strachy married the yeoman of the wardrobe.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: Fie on him, Jezebel!

speeches.speaker: FABIAN
speeches.text: O, peace, now he’s deeply in. Look how imagination blows him.

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: Having been three months married to her, sitting in my state—

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: O, for a stone-bow, to hit him in the eye!

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: Calling my officers about me, in my branched velvet gown, having come from a daybed where I have left Olivia sleeping—

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Fire and brimstone!

speeches.speaker: FABIAN
speeches.text: O, peace, peace!

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: And then to have the humor of state; and after a demure travel of regard, telling them I know my place, as I would they should do theirs, to ask for my kinsman Toby—

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Bolts and shackles!

speeches.speaker: FABIAN
speeches.text: O, peace, peace, peace! Now, now.

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: Seven of my people, with an obedient start, make out for him. I frown the while, and perchance wind up my watch, or play with my—some rich jewel. Toby approaches; curtsies there to me—

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Shall this fellow live?

speeches.speaker: FABIAN
speeches.text: Though our silence be drawn from us with cars, yet peace!

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: I extend my hand to him thus, quenching my familiar smile with an austere regard of control—

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: And does not Toby take you a blow o’ the lips then?

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: Saying, “Cousin Toby, my fortunes, having cast me on your niece, give me this prerogative of speech—”

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: What, what?

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: “You must amend your drunkenness.”

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Out, scab!

speeches.speaker: FABIAN
speeches.text: Nay, patience, or we break the sinews of our plot!

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: “Besides, you waste the treasure of your time with a foolish knight—”

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: That’s me, I warrant you.

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: “One Sir Andrew.”

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: I knew ’twas I, for many do call me fool.

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: What employment have we here?

speeches.speaker: FABIAN
speeches.text: Now is the woodcock near the gin.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: O, peace, and the spirit of humors intimate reading aloud to him.

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: By my life, this is my lady’s hand! These be her very, her, and her, and thus she makes her great. It is in contempt of question her hand.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: Her, her, and her. Why that?

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: To the unknown beloved, this, and my good wishes—Her very phrases! By your leave, wax. Soft. And the impressure her Lucrece, with which she uses to seal—’tis my lady! To whom should this be?

speeches.speaker: FABIAN
speeches.text: This wins him, liver and all.

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: Jove knows I love, But who? Lips, do not move; No man must know. “No man must know.” What follows? The numbers altered. “No man must know.” If this should be thee, Malvolio!

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Marry, hang thee, brock!

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: I may command where I adore, But silence, like a Lucrece knife, With bloodless stroke my heart doth gore; M.O.A.I. doth sway my life.

speeches.speaker: FABIAN
speeches.text: A fustian riddle!

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Excellent wench, say I.

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: “M.O.A.I. doth sway my life.” Nay, but first let me see, let me see, let me see.

speeches.speaker: FABIAN
speeches.text: What dish o’ poison has she dressed him!

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: And with what wing the staniel checks at it!

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: “I may command where I adore.” Why, she may command me; I serve her; she is my lady. Why, this is evident to any formal capacity. There is no obstruction in this. And the end—what should that alphabetical position portend? If I could make that resemble something in me! Softly! “M.O.A.I.”—

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: O, ay, make up that.—He is now at a cold scent.

speeches.speaker: FABIAN
speeches.text: Sowter will cry upon ’t for all this, though it be as rank as a fox.

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: “M”—Malvolio. “M”—why, that begins my name!

speeches.speaker: FABIAN
speeches.text: Did not I say he would work it out? The cur is excellent at faults.

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: “M.” But then there is no consonancy in the sequel that suffers under probation. “A” should follow, but “O” does.

speeches.speaker: FABIAN
speeches.text: And “O” shall end, I hope.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Ay, or I’ll cudgel him and make him cry “O.”

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: And then “I” comes behind.

speeches.speaker: FABIAN
speeches.text: Ay, an you had any eye behind you, you might see more detraction at your heels than fortunes before you.

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: “M.O.A.I.” This simulation is not as the former, and yet to crush this a little, it would bow to me, for every one of these letters are in my name. Soft, here follows prose. If this fall into thy hand, revolve. In my stars I am above thee, but be not afraid of greatness. Some are born great, some achieve greatness, and some have greatness thrust upon ’em. Thy fates open their hands. Let thy blood and spirit embrace them. And, to inure thyself to what thou art like to be, cast thy humble slough and appear fresh. Be opposite with a kinsman, surly with servants. Let thy tongue tang arguments of state. Put thyself into the trick of singularity. She thus advises thee that sighs for thee. Remember who commended thy yellow stockings and wished to see thee ever cross-gartered. I say, remember. Go to, thou art made, if thou desir’st to be so. If not, let me see thee a steward still, the fellow of servants, and not worthy to touch Fortune’s fingers. Farewell. She that would alter services with thee, The Fortunate-Unhappy. Daylight and champian discovers not more! This is open. I will be proud, I will read politic authors, I will baffle Sir Toby, I will wash off gross acquaintance, I will be point-devise the very man. I do not now fool myself, to let imagination jade me; for every reason excites to this, that my lady loves me. She did commend my yellow stockings of late, she did praise my leg being cross-gartered, and in this she manifests herself to my love and, with a kind of injunction, drives me to these habits of her liking. I thank my stars, I am happy. I will be strange, stout, in yellow stockings, and cross-gartered, even with the swiftness of putting on. Jove and my stars be praised! Here is yet a postscript. Thou canst not choose but know who I am. If thou entertain’st my love, let it appear in thy smiling; thy smiles become thee well. Therefore in my presence still smile, dear my sweet, I prithee. Jove, I thank thee! I will smile. I will do everything that thou wilt have me.

speeches.speaker: FABIAN
speeches.text: I will not give my part of this sport for a pension of thousands to be paid from the Sophy.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: I could marry this wench for this device.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: So could I too.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: And ask no other dowry with her but such another jest.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: Nor I neither.

speeches.speaker: FABIAN
speeches.text: Here comes my noble gull-catcher.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Wilt thou set thy foot o’ my neck?

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: Or o’ mine either?

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Shall I play my freedom at tray-trip and become thy bondslave?

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: I’ faith, or I either?

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Why, thou hast put him in such a dream that when the image of it leaves him he must run mad.

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: Nay, but say true, does it work upon him?

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Like aqua vitae with a midwife.

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: If you will then see the fruits of the sport, mark his first approach before my lady. He will come to her in yellow stockings, and ’tis a color she abhors, and cross-gartered, a fashion she detests; and he will smile upon her, which will now be so unsuitable to her disposition, being addicted to a melancholy as she is, that it cannot but turn him into a notable contempt. If you will see it, follow me.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: To the gates of Tartar, thou most excellent devil of wit!

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: I’ll make one, too.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: Save thee, friend, and thy music. Dost thou live by thy tabor?

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: No, sir, I live by the church.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: Art thou a churchman?

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: No such matter, sir. I do live by the church, for I do live at my house, and my house doth stand by the church.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: So thou mayst say the king lies by a beggar if a beggar dwell near him, or the church stands by thy tabor if thy tabor stand by the church.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: You have said, sir. To see this age! A sentence is but a chev’ril glove to a good wit. How quickly the wrong side may be turned outward!

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: Nay, that’s certain. They that dally nicely with words may quickly make them wanton.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: I would therefore my sister had had no name, sir.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: Why, man?

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Why, sir, her name’s a word, and to dally with that word might make my sister wanton. But, indeed, words are very rascals since bonds disgraced them.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: Thy reason, man?

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Troth, sir, I can yield you none without words, and words are grown so false I am loath to prove reason with them.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: I warrant thou art a merry fellow and car’st for nothing.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Not so, sir. I do care for something. But in my conscience, sir, I do not care for you. If that be to care for nothing, sir, I would it would make you invisible.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: Art not thou the Lady Olivia’s Fool?

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: No, indeed, sir. The Lady Olivia has no folly. She will keep no Fool, sir, till she be married, and Fools are as like husbands as pilchers are to herrings: the husband’s the bigger. I am indeed not her Fool but her corrupter of words.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: I saw thee late at the Count Orsino’s.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Foolery, sir, does walk about the orb like the sun; it shines everywhere. I would be sorry, sir, but the Fool should be as oft with your master as with my mistress. I think I saw your Wisdom there.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: Nay, an thou pass upon me, I’ll no more with thee. Hold, there’s expenses for thee.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Now Jove, in his next commodity of hair, send thee a beard!

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: By my troth I’ll tell thee, I am almost sick for one, though I would not have it grow on my chin.—Is thy lady within?

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Would not a pair of these have bred, sir?

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: Yes, being kept together and put to use.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: I would play Lord Pandarus of Phrygia, sir, to bring a Cressida to this Troilus.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: I understand you, sir. ’Tis well begged.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: The matter I hope is not great, sir, begging but a beggar: Cressida was a beggar. My lady is within, sir. I will conster to them whence you come. Who you are and what you would are out of my welkin—I might say “element,” but the word is overworn.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: This fellow is wise enough to play the Fool, And to do that well craves a kind of wit. He must observe their mood on whom he jests, The quality of persons, and the time, And, like the haggard, check at every feather That comes before his eye. This is a practice As full of labor as a wise man’s art: For folly that he wisely shows is fit; But wise men, folly-fall’n, quite taint their wit.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Save you, gentleman.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: And you, sir.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: Dieu vous garde, monsieur.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: Et vous aussi. Votre serviteur!

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: I hope, sir, you are, and I am yours.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Will you encounter the house? My niece is desirous you should enter, if your trade be to her.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: I am bound to your niece, sir; I mean, she is the list of my voyage.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Taste your legs, sir; put them to motion.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: My legs do better understand me, sir, than I understand what you mean by bidding me taste my legs.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: I mean, to go, sir, to enter.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: I will answer you with gait and entrance—but we are prevented. Most excellent accomplished lady, the heavens rain odors on you!

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: That youth’s a rare courtier. “Rain odors,” well.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: My matter hath no voice, lady, but to your own most pregnant and vouchsafed ear.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: “Odors,” “pregnant,” and “vouchsafed.” I’ll get ’em all three all ready.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Let the garden door be shut, and leave me to my hearing. Give me your hand, sir.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: My duty, madam, and most humble service.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: What is your name?

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: Cesario is your servant’s name, fair princess.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: My servant, sir? ’Twas never merry world Since lowly feigning was called compliment. You’re servant to the Count Orsino, youth.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: And he is yours, and his must needs be yours. Your servant’s servant is your servant, madam.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: For him, I think not on him. For his thoughts, Would they were blanks rather than filled with me.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: Madam, I come to whet your gentle thoughts On his behalf.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: O, by your leave, I pray you. I bade you never speak again of him. But would you undertake another suit, I had rather hear you to solicit that Than music from the spheres.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: Dear lady—

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Give me leave, beseech you. I did send, After the last enchantment you did here, A ring in chase of you. So did I abuse Myself, my servant, and, I fear me, you. Under your hard construction must I sit, To force that on you in a shameful cunning Which you knew none of yours. What might you think? Have you not set mine honor at the stake And baited it with all th’ unmuzzled thoughts That tyrannous heart can think? To one of your receiving Enough is shown. A cypress, not a bosom, Hides my heart. So, let me hear you speak.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: I pity you.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: That’s a degree to love.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: No, not a grize, for ’tis a vulgar proof That very oft we pity enemies.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Why then methinks ’tis time to smile again. O world, how apt the poor are to be proud! If one should be a prey, how much the better To fall before the lion than the wolf. The clock upbraids me with the waste of time. Be not afraid, good youth, I will not have you. And yet when wit and youth is come to harvest, Your wife is like to reap a proper man. There lies your way, due west.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: Then westward ho! Grace and good disposition attend your Ladyship. You’ll nothing, madam, to my lord by me?

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Stay. I prithee, tell me what thou think’st of me.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: That you do think you are not what you are.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: If I think so, I think the same of you.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: Then think you right. I am not what I am.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: I would you were as I would have you be.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: Would it be better, madam, than I am? I wish it might, for now I am your fool.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: O, what a deal of scorn looks beautiful In the contempt and anger of his lip! A murd’rous guilt shows not itself more soon Than love that would seem hid. Love’s night is noon.— Cesario, by the roses of the spring, By maidhood, honor, truth, and everything, I love thee so, that, maugre all thy pride, Nor wit nor reason can my passion hide. Do not extort thy reasons from this clause, For that I woo, thou therefore hast no cause; But rather reason thus with reason fetter: Love sought is good, but given unsought is better.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: By innocence I swear, and by my youth, I have one heart, one bosom, and one truth, And that no woman has, nor never none Shall mistress be of it, save I alone. And so adieu, good madam. Nevermore Will I my master’s tears to you deplore.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Yet come again, for thou perhaps mayst move That heart, which now abhors, to like his love.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: No, faith, I’ll not stay a jot longer.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Thy reason, dear venom, give thy reason.

speeches.speaker: FABIAN
speeches.text: You must needs yield your reason, Sir Andrew.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: Marry, I saw your niece do more favors to the Count’s servingman than ever she bestowed upon me. I saw ’t i’ th’ orchard.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Did she see thee the while, old boy? Tell me that.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: As plain as I see you now.

speeches.speaker: FABIAN
speeches.text: This was a great argument of love in her toward you.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: ’Slight, will you make an ass o’ me?

speeches.speaker: FABIAN
speeches.text: I will prove it legitimate, sir, upon the oaths of judgment and reason.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: And they have been grand-jurymen since before Noah was a sailor.

speeches.speaker: FABIAN
speeches.text: She did show favor to the youth in your sight only to exasperate you, to awake your dormouse valor, to put fire in your heart and brimstone in your liver. You should then have accosted her, and with some excellent jests, fire-new from the mint, you should have banged the youth into dumbness. This was looked for at your hand, and this was balked. The double gilt of this opportunity you let time wash off, and you are now sailed into the north of my lady’s opinion, where you will hang like an icicle on a Dutchman’s beard, unless you do redeem it by some laudable attempt either of valor or policy.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: An ’t be any way, it must be with valor, for policy I hate. I had as lief be a Brownist as a politician.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Why, then, build me thy fortunes upon the basis of valor. Challenge me the Count’s youth to fight with him. Hurt him in eleven places. My niece shall take note of it, and assure thyself there is no love-broker in the world can more prevail in man’s commendation with woman than report of valor.

speeches.speaker: FABIAN
speeches.text: There is no way but this, Sir Andrew.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: Will either of you bear me a challenge to him?

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Go, write it in a martial hand. Be curst and brief. It is no matter how witty, so it be eloquent and full of invention. Taunt him with the license of ink. If thou “” him some thrice, it shall not be amiss, and as many lies as will lie in thy sheet of paper, although the sheet were big enough for the bed of Ware in England, set ’em down. Go, about it. Let there be gall enough in thy ink, though thou write with a goose-pen, no matter. About it.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: Where shall I find you?

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: We’ll call thee at the cubiculo. Go.

speeches.speaker: FABIAN
speeches.text: This is a dear manikin to you, Sir Toby.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: I have been dear to him, lad, some two thousand strong or so.

speeches.speaker: FABIAN
speeches.text: We shall have a rare letter from him. But you’ll not deliver ’t?

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Never trust me, then. And by all means stir on the youth to an answer. I think oxen and wainropes cannot hale them together. For Andrew, if he were opened and you find so much blood in his liver as will clog the foot of a flea, I’ll eat the rest of th’ anatomy.

speeches.speaker: FABIAN
speeches.text: And his opposite, the youth, bears in his visage no great presage of cruelty.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Look where the youngest wren of mine comes.

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: If you desire the spleen, and will laugh yourselves into stitches, follow me. Yond gull Malvolio is turned heathen, a very renegado; for there is no Christian that means to be saved by believing rightly can ever believe such impossible passages of grossness. He’s in yellow stockings.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: And cross-gartered?

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: Most villainously, like a pedant that keeps a school i’ th’ church. I have dogged him like his murderer. He does obey every point of the letter that I dropped to betray him. He does smile his face into more lines than is in the new map with the augmentation of the Indies. You have not seen such a thing as ’tis. I can hardly forbear hurling things at him. I know my lady will strike him. If she do, he’ll smile and take ’t for a great favor.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Come, bring us, bring us where he is.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
speeches.text: I would not by my will have troubled you, But, since you make your pleasure of your pains, I will no further chide you.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: I could not stay behind you. My desire, More sharp than filèd steel, did spur me forth; And not all love to see you, though so much As might have drawn one to a longer voyage, But jealousy what might befall your travel, Being skill-less in these parts, which to a stranger, Unguided and unfriended, often prove Rough and unhospitable. My willing love, The rather by these arguments of fear, Set forth in your pursuit.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
