speeches.text: My kind Antonio, I can no other answer make but thanks, And thanks, and ever thanks; and oft good turns Are shuffled off with such uncurrent pay. But were my worth, as is my conscience, firm, You should find better dealing. What’s to do? Shall we go see the relics of this town?

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Tomorrow, sir. Best first go see your lodging.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
speeches.text: I am not weary, and ’tis long to night. I pray you, let us satisfy our eyes With the memorials and the things of fame That do renown this city.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Would you’d pardon me. I do not without danger walk these streets. Once in a sea fight ’gainst the Count his galleys I did some service, of such note indeed That were I ta’en here it would scarce be answered.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
speeches.text: Belike you slew great number of his people?

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Th’ offense is not of such a bloody nature, Albeit the quality of the time and quarrel Might well have given us bloody argument. It might have since been answered in repaying What we took from them, which, for traffic’s sake, Most of our city did. Only myself stood out, For which, if I be lapsèd in this place, I shall pay dear.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
speeches.text: Do not then walk too open.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: It doth not fit me. Hold, sir, here’s my purse. In the south suburbs, at the Elephant, Is best to lodge. I will bespeak our diet Whiles you beguile the time and feed your knowledge With viewing of the town. There shall you have me.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
speeches.text: Why I your purse?

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Haply your eye shall light upon some toy You have desire to purchase, and your store, I think, is not for idle markets, sir.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
speeches.text: I’ll be your purse-bearer and leave you For an hour.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: To th’ Elephant.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
speeches.text: I do remember.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: I have sent after him. He says he’ll come. How shall I feast him? What bestow of him? For youth is bought more oft than begged or borrowed. I speak too loud.— Where’s Malvolio? He is sad and civil And suits well for a servant with my fortunes. Where is Malvolio?

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: He’s coming, madam, but in very strange manner. He is sure possessed, madam.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Why, what’s the matter? Does he rave?

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: No, madam, he does nothing but smile. Your Ladyship were best to have some guard about you if he come, for sure the man is tainted in ’s wits.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Go call him hither. I am as mad as he, If sad and merry madness equal be. How now, Malvolio?

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: Sweet lady, ho, ho!

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Smil’st thou? I sent for thee upon a sad occasion.

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: Sad, lady? I could be sad. This does make some obstruction in the blood, this cross-gartering, but what of that? If it please the eye of one, it is with me as the very true sonnet is: “Please one, and please all.”

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Why, how dost thou, man? What is the matter with thee?

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: Not black in my mind, though yellow in my legs. It did come to his hands, and commands shall be executed. I think we do know the sweet Roman hand.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Wilt thou go to bed, Malvolio?

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: To bed? “Ay, sweetheart, and I’ll come to thee.”

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: God comfort thee! Why dost thou smile so, and kiss thy hand so oft?

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: How do you, Malvolio?

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: At your request? Yes, nightingales answer daws!

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: Why appear you with this ridiculous boldness before my lady?

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: “Be not afraid of greatness.” ’Twas well writ.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: What mean’st thou by that, Malvolio?

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: “Some are born great—”

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Ha?

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: “Some achieve greatness—”

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: What sayst thou?

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: “And some have greatness thrust upon them.”

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Heaven restore thee!

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: “Remember who commended thy yellow stockings—”

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Thy yellow stockings?

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: “And wished to see thee cross-gartered.”

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Cross-gartered?

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: “Go to, thou art made, if thou desir’st to be so—”

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Am I made?

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: “If not, let me see thee a servant still.”

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Why, this is very midsummer madness!

speeches.speaker: SERVANT
speeches.text: Madam, the young gentleman of the Count Orsino’s is returned. I could hardly entreat him back. He attends your Ladyship’s pleasure.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: I’ll come to him. Good Maria, let this fellow be looked to. Where’s my Cousin Toby? Let some of my people have a special care of him. I would not have him miscarry for the half of my dowry.

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: O ho, do you come near me now? No worse man than Sir Toby to look to me. This concurs directly with the letter. She sends him on purpose that I may appear stubborn to him, for she incites me to that in the letter: “Cast thy humble slough,” says she. “Be opposite with a kinsman, surly with servants; let thy tongue tang with arguments of state; put thyself into the trick of singularity,” and consequently sets down the manner how: as, a sad face, a reverend carriage, a slow tongue, in the habit of some Sir of note, and so forth. I have limed her, but it is Jove’s doing, and Jove make me thankful! And when she went away now, “Let this fellow be looked to.” “Fellow!” Not “Malvolio,” nor after my degree, but “fellow.” Why, everything adheres together, that no dram of a scruple, no scruple of a scruple, no obstacle, no incredulous or unsafe circumstance—what can be said? Nothing that can be can come between me and the full prospect of my hopes. Well, Jove, not I, is the doer of this, and he is to be thanked.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Which way is he, in the name of sanctity? If all the devils of hell be drawn in little, and Legion himself possessed him, yet I’ll speak to him.

speeches.speaker: FABIAN
speeches.text: Here he is, here he is.—How is ’t with you, sir? How is ’t with you, man?

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: Go off, I discard you. Let me enjoy my private. Go off.

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: Lo, how hollow the fiend speaks within him! Did not I tell you? Sir Toby, my lady prays you to have a care of him.

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: Aha, does she so?

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Go to, go to! Peace, peace. We must deal gently with him. Let me alone.—How do you, Malvolio? How is ’t with you? What, man, defy the devil! Consider, he’s an enemy to mankind.

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: Do you know what you say?

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: La you, an you speak ill of the devil, how he takes it at heart! Pray God he be not bewitched!

speeches.speaker: FABIAN
speeches.text: Carry his water to th’ wisewoman.

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: Marry, and it shall be done tomorrow morning if I live. My lady would not lose him for more than I’ll say.

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: How now, mistress?

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: O Lord!

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Prithee, hold thy peace. This is not the way. Do you not see you move him? Let me alone with him.

speeches.speaker: FABIAN
speeches.text: No way but gentleness, gently, gently. The fiend is rough and will not be roughly used.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Why, how now, my bawcock? How dost thou, chuck?

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: Sir!

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Ay, biddy, come with me.—What, man, ’tis not for gravity to play at cherry-pit with Satan. Hang him, foul collier!

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: Get him to say his prayers, good Sir Toby; get him to pray.

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: My prayers, minx?

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: No, I warrant you, he will not hear of godliness.

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: Go hang yourselves all! You are idle, shallow things. I am not of your element. You shall know more hereafter.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Is ’t possible?

speeches.speaker: FABIAN
speeches.text: If this were played upon a stage now, I could condemn it as an improbable fiction.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: His very genius hath taken the infection of the device, man.

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: Nay, pursue him now, lest the device take air and taint.

speeches.speaker: FABIAN
speeches.text: Why, we shall make him mad indeed.

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: The house will be the quieter.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Come, we’ll have him in a dark room and bound. My niece is already in the belief that he’s mad. We may carry it thus, for our pleasure and his penance, till our very pastime, tired out of breath, prompt us to have mercy on him, at which time we will bring the device to the bar and crown thee for a finder of madmen. But see, but see!

speeches.speaker: FABIAN
speeches.text: More matter for a May morning.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: Here’s the challenge. Read it. I warrant there’s vinegar and pepper in ’t.

speeches.speaker: FABIAN
speeches.text: Is ’t so saucy?

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: Ay, is ’t. I warrant him. Do but read.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Give me. Youth, whatsoever thou art, thou art but a scurvy fellow.

speeches.speaker: FABIAN
speeches.text: Good, and valiant.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Wonder not nor admire not in thy mind why I do call thee so, for I will show thee no reason for ’t.

speeches.speaker: FABIAN
speeches.text: A good note, that keeps you from the blow of the law.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Thou com’st to the Lady Olivia, and in my sight she uses thee kindly. But thou liest in thy throat; that is not the matter I challenge thee for.

speeches.speaker: FABIAN
speeches.text: Very brief, and to exceeding good sense—less.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: I will waylay thee going home, where if it be thy chance to kill me—

speeches.speaker: FABIAN
speeches.text: Good.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Thou kill’st me like a rogue and a villain.

speeches.speaker: FABIAN
speeches.text: Still you keep o’ th’ windy side of the law. Good.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Fare thee well, and God have mercy upon one of our souls. He may have mercy upon mine, but my hope is better, and so look to thyself. Thy friend, as thou usest him, and thy sworn enemy, Andrew Aguecheek. If this letter move him not, his legs cannot. I’ll give ’t him.

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: You may have very fit occasion for ’t. He is now in some commerce with my lady and will by and by depart.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Go, Sir Andrew. Scout me for him at the corner of the orchard like a bum-baily. So soon as ever thou seest him, draw, and as thou draw’st, swear horrible, for it comes to pass oft that a terrible oath, with a swaggering accent sharply twanged off, gives manhood more approbation than ever proof itself would have earned him. Away!

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: Nay, let me alone for swearing.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Now will not I deliver his letter, for the behavior of the young gentleman gives him out to be of good capacity and breeding; his employment between his lord and my niece confirms no less. Therefore, this letter, being so excellently ignorant, will breed no terror in the youth. He will find it comes from a clodpoll. But, sir, I will deliver his challenge by word of mouth, set upon Aguecheek a notable report of valor, and drive the gentleman (as I know his youth will aptly receive it) into a most hideous opinion of his rage, skill, fury, and impetuosity. This will so fright them both that they will kill one another by the look, like cockatrices.

speeches.speaker: FABIAN
speeches.text: Here he comes with your niece. Give them way till he take leave, and presently after him.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: I will meditate the while upon some horrid message for a challenge.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: I have said too much unto a heart of stone And laid mine honor too unchary on ’t. There’s something in me that reproves my fault, But such a headstrong potent fault it is That it but mocks reproof.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: With the same ’havior that your passion bears Goes on my master’s griefs.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Here, wear this jewel for me. ’Tis my picture. Refuse it not. It hath no tongue to vex you. And I beseech you come again tomorrow. What shall you ask of me that I’ll deny, That honor, saved, may upon asking give?

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: Nothing but this: your true love for my master.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: How with mine honor may I give him that Which I have given to you?

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: I will acquit you.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Well, come again tomorrow. Fare thee well. A fiend like thee might bear my soul to hell.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Gentleman, God save thee.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: And you, sir.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: That defense thou hast, betake thee to ’t. Of what nature the wrongs are thou hast done him, I know not, but thy intercepter, full of despite, bloody as the hunter, attends thee at the orchard end. Dismount thy tuck, be yare in thy preparation, for thy assailant is quick, skillful, and deadly.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: You mistake, sir. I am sure no man hath any quarrel to me. My remembrance is very free and clear from any image of offense done to any man.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: You’ll find it otherwise, I assure you. Therefore, if you hold your life at any price, betake you to your guard, for your opposite hath in him what youth, strength, skill, and wrath can furnish man withal.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: I pray you, sir, what is he?

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: He is knight dubbed with unhatched rapier and on carpet consideration, but he is a devil in private brawl. Souls and bodies hath he divorced three, and his incensement at this moment is so implacable that satisfaction can be none but by pangs of death and sepulcher. “Hob, nob” is his word; “give ’t or take ’t.”

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: I will return again into the house and desire some conduct of the lady. I am no fighter. I have heard of some kind of men that put quarrels purposely on others to taste their valor. Belike this is a man of that quirk.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Sir, no. His indignation derives itself out of a very competent injury. Therefore get you on and give him his desire. Back you shall not to the house, unless you undertake that with me which with as much safety you might answer him. Therefore on, or strip your sword stark naked, for meddle you must, that’s certain, or forswear to wear iron about you.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: This is as uncivil as strange. I beseech you, do me this courteous office, as to know of the knight what my offense to him is. It is something of my negligence, nothing of my purpose.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: I will do so.—Signior Fabian, stay you by this gentleman till my return.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: Pray you, sir, do you know of this matter?

speeches.speaker: FABIAN
speeches.text: I know the knight is incensed against you even to a mortal arbitrament, but nothing of the circumstance more.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: I beseech you, what manner of man is he?

speeches.speaker: FABIAN
speeches.text: Nothing of that wonderful promise, to read him by his form, as you are like to find him in the proof of his valor. He is indeed, sir, the most skillful, bloody, and fatal opposite that you could possibly have found in any part of Illyria. Will you walk towards him? I will make your peace with him if I can.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: I shall be much bound to you for ’t. I am one that had rather go with Sir Priest than Sir Knight, I care not who knows so much of my mettle.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Why, man, he’s a very devil. I have not seen such a firago. I had a pass with him, rapier, scabbard, and all, and he gives me the stuck-in with such a mortal motion that it is inevitable; and on the answer, he pays you as surely as your feet hits the ground they step on. They say he has been fencer to the Sophy.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: Pox on ’t! I’ll not meddle with him.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Ay, but he will not now be pacified. Fabian can scarce hold him yonder.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: Plague on ’t! An I thought he had been valiant, and so cunning in fence, I’d have seen him damned ere I’d have challenged him. Let him let the matter slip, and I’ll give him my horse, gray Capilet.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: I’ll make the motion. Stand here, make a good show on ’t. This shall end without the perdition of souls. Marry, I’ll ride your horse as well as I ride you. I have his horse to take up the quarrel. I have persuaded him the youth’s a devil.

speeches.speaker: FABIAN
speeches.text: He is as horribly conceited of him, and pants and looks pale as if a bear were at his heels.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: There’s no remedy, sir; he will fight with you for ’s oath sake. Marry, he hath better bethought him of his quarrel, and he finds that now scarce to be worth talking of. Therefore, draw for the supportance of his vow. He protests he will not hurt you.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: Pray God defend me! A little thing would make me tell them how much I lack of a man.

speeches.speaker: FABIAN
speeches.text: Give ground if you see him furious.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Come, Sir Andrew, there’s no remedy. The gentleman will, for his honor’s sake, have one bout with you. He cannot by the duello avoid it. But he has promised me, as he is a gentleman and a soldier, he will not hurt you. Come on, to ’t.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: Pray God he keep his oath!

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: I do assure you ’tis against my will.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Put up your sword. If this young gentleman Have done offense, I take the fault on me. If you offend him, I for him defy you.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: You, sir? Why, what are you?

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: One, sir, that for his love dares yet do more Than you have heard him brag to you he will.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Nay, if you be an undertaker, I am for you.

speeches.speaker: FABIAN
speeches.text: O, good Sir Toby, hold! Here come the officers.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: I’ll be with you anon.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: Pray, sir, put your sword up, if you please.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: Marry, will I, sir. And for that I promised you, I’ll be as good as my word. He will bear you easily, and reins well.

speeches.speaker: FIRST OFFICER
speeches.text: This is the man. Do thy office.

speeches.speaker: SECOND OFFICER
speeches.text: Antonio, I arrest thee at the suit of Count Orsino.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: You do mistake me, sir.

speeches.speaker: FIRST OFFICER
speeches.text: No, sir, no jot. I know your favor well, Though now you have no sea-cap on your head.— Take him away. He knows I know him well.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: I must obey. This comes with seeking you. But there’s no remedy. I shall answer it. What will you do, now my necessity Makes me to ask you for my purse? It grieves me Much more for what I cannot do for you Than what befalls myself. You stand amazed, But be of comfort.

speeches.speaker: SECOND OFFICER
speeches.text: Come, sir, away.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: I must entreat of you some of that money.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: What money, sir? For the fair kindness you have showed me here, And part being prompted by your present trouble, Out of my lean and low ability I’ll lend you something. My having is not much. I’ll make division of my present with you. Hold, there’s half my coffer.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Will you deny me now? Is ’t possible that my deserts to you Can lack persuasion? Do not tempt my misery, Lest that it make me so unsound a man As to upbraid you with those kindnesses That I have done for you.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: I know of none, Nor know I you by voice or any feature. I hate ingratitude more in a man Than lying, vainness, babbling drunkenness, Or any taint of vice whose strong corruption Inhabits our frail blood—

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: O heavens themselves!

speeches.speaker: SECOND OFFICER
speeches.text: Come, sir, I pray you go.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Let me speak a little. This youth that you see here I snatched one half out of the jaws of death, Relieved him with such sanctity of love, And to his image, which methought did promise Most venerable worth, did I devotion.

speeches.speaker: FIRST OFFICER
speeches.text: What’s that to us? The time goes by. Away!

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: But O, how vile an idol proves this god! Thou hast, Sebastian, done good feature shame. In nature there’s no blemish but the mind; None can be called deformed but the unkind. Virtue is beauty, but the beauteous evil Are empty trunks o’erflourished by the devil.

speeches.speaker: FIRST OFFICER
speeches.text: The man grows mad. Away with him.—Come, come, sir.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Lead me on.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: Methinks his words do from such passion fly That he believes himself; so do not I. Prove true, imagination, O, prove true, That I, dear brother, be now ta’en for you!

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Come hither, knight; come hither, Fabian. We’ll whisper o’er a couplet or two of most sage saws.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: He named Sebastian. I my brother know Yet living in my glass. Even such and so In favor was my brother, and he went Still in this fashion, color, ornament, For him I imitate. O, if it prove, Tempests are kind, and salt waves fresh in love!

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: A very dishonest, paltry boy, and more a coward than a hare. His dishonesty appears in leaving his friend here in necessity and denying him; and for his cowardship, ask Fabian.

speeches.speaker: FABIAN
speeches.text: A coward, a most devout coward, religious in it.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: ’Slid, I’ll after him again and beat him.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Do, cuff him soundly, but never draw thy sword.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: An I do not—

speeches.speaker: FABIAN
speeches.text: Come, let’s see the event.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: I dare lay any money ’twill be nothing yet.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Will you make me believe that I am not sent for you?

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
speeches.text: Go to, go to, thou art a foolish fellow. Let me be clear of thee.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Well held out, i’ faith. No, I do not know you, nor I am not sent to you by my lady to bid you come speak with her, nor your name is not Master Cesario, nor this is not my nose neither. Nothing that is so is so.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
speeches.text: I prithee, vent thy folly somewhere else. Thou know’st not me.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Vent my folly? He has heard that word of some great man and now applies it to a Fool. Vent my folly? I am afraid this great lubber the world will prove a cockney. I prithee now, ungird thy strangeness and tell me what I shall vent to my lady. Shall I vent to her that thou art coming?

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
speeches.text: I prithee, foolish Greek, depart from me. There’s money for thee. If you tarry longer, I shall give worse payment.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: By my troth, thou hast an open hand. These wise men that give Fools money get themselves a good report—after fourteen years’ purchase.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: Now, sir, have I met you again? There’s for you.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
speeches.text: Why, there’s for thee, and there, and there.—Are all the people mad?

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Hold, sir, or I’ll throw your dagger o’er the house.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: This will I tell my lady straight. I would not be in some of your coats for twopence.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Come on, sir, hold!

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: Nay, let him alone. I’ll go another way to work with him. I’ll have an action of battery against him, if there be any law in Illyria. Though I struck him first, yet it’s no matter for that.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
speeches.text: Let go thy hand!

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Come, sir, I will not let you go. Come, my young soldier, put up your iron. You are well fleshed. Come on.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
speeches.text: I will be free from thee. What wouldst thou now? If thou dar’st tempt me further, draw thy sword.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: What, what? Nay, then, I must have an ounce or two of this malapert blood from you.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Hold, Toby! On thy life I charge thee, hold!

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Madam.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Will it be ever thus? Ungracious wretch, Fit for the mountains and the barbarous caves, Where manners ne’er were preached! Out of my sight!— Be not offended, dear Cesario.— Rudesby, begone! I prithee, gentle friend, Let thy fair wisdom, not thy passion, sway In this uncivil and unjust extent Against thy peace. Go with me to my house, And hear thou there how many fruitless pranks This ruffian hath botched up, that thou thereby Mayst smile at this. Thou shalt not choose but go. Do not deny. Beshrew his soul for me! He started one poor heart of mine, in thee.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
speeches.text: What relish is in this? How runs the stream? Or I am mad, or else this is a dream. Let fancy still my sense in Lethe steep; If it be thus to dream, still let me sleep!

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Nay, come, I prithee. Would thou ’dst be ruled by me!

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
speeches.text: Madam, I will.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: O, say so, and so be!

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: Nay, I prithee, put on this gown and this beard; make him believe thou art Sir Topas the curate. Do it quickly. I’ll call Sir Toby the whilst.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Well, I’ll put it on and I will dissemble myself in ’t, and I would I were the first that ever dissembled in such a gown. I am not tall enough to become the function well, nor lean enough to be thought a good student, but to be said an honest man and a good housekeeper goes as fairly as to say a careful man and a great scholar. The competitors enter.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Jove bless thee, Master Parson.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Bonos dies, Sir Toby; for, as the old hermit of Prague, that never saw pen and ink, very wittily said to a niece of King Gorboduc “That that is, is,” so I, being Master Parson, am Master Parson; for what is “that” but “that” and “is” but “is”?

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: To him, Sir Topas.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: What ho, I say! Peace in this prison!

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: The knave counterfeits well. A good knave.

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: Who calls there?

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Sir Topas the curate, who comes to visit Malvolio the lunatic.

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: Sir Topas, Sir Topas, good Sir Topas, go to my lady—

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Out, hyperbolical fiend! How vexest thou this man! Talkest thou nothing but of ladies?

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Well said, Master Parson.

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: Sir Topas, never was man thus wronged. Good Sir Topas, do not think I am mad. They have laid me here in hideous darkness—

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Fie, thou dishonest Satan! I call thee by the most modest terms, for I am one of those gentle ones that will use the devil himself with courtesy. Sayst thou that house is dark?

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: As hell, Sir Topas.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Why, it hath bay windows transparent as barricadoes, and the clerestories toward the south-north are as lustrous as ebony; and yet complainest thou of obstruction?

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: I am not mad, Sir Topas. I say to you this house is dark.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Madman, thou errest. I say there is no darkness but ignorance, in which thou art more puzzled than the Egyptians in their fog.

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: I say this house is as dark as ignorance, though ignorance were as dark as hell. And I say there was never man thus abused. I am no more mad than you are. Make the trial of it in any constant question.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: What is the opinion of Pythagoras concerning wildfowl?

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: That the soul of our grandam might haply inhabit a bird.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: What thinkst thou of his opinion?

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: I think nobly of the soul, and no way approve his opinion.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Fare thee well. Remain thou still in darkness. Thou shalt hold th’ opinion of Pythagoras ere I will allow of thy wits, and fear to kill a woodcock lest thou dispossess the soul of thy grandam. Fare thee well.

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: Sir Topas, Sir Topas!

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: My most exquisite Sir Topas!

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Nay, I am for all waters.

speeches.speaker: MARIA
speeches.text: Thou mightst have done this without thy beard and gown. He sees thee not.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: To him in thine own voice, and bring me word how thou find’st him. I would we were well rid of this knavery. If he may be conveniently delivered, I would he were, for I am now so far in offense with my niece that I cannot pursue with any safety this sport the upshot. Come by and by to my chamber.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Hey, Robin, jolly Robin, Tell me how thy lady does.

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: Fool!

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: My lady is unkind, perdy.

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: Fool!

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Alas, why is she so?

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: Fool, I say!

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: She loves another— Who calls, ha?

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: Good fool, as ever thou wilt deserve well at my hand, help me to a candle, and pen, ink, and paper. As I am a gentleman, I will live to be thankful to thee for ’t.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Master Malvolio?

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: Ay, good Fool.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Alas, sir, how fell you besides your five wits?

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: Fool, there was never man so notoriously abused. I am as well in my wits, Fool, as thou art.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: But as well? Then you are mad indeed, if you be no better in your wits than a Fool.

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: They have here propertied me, keep me in darkness, send ministers to me—asses!—and do all they can to face me out of my wits.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Advise you what you say. The minister is here. Malvolio, Malvolio, thy wits the heavens restore. Endeavor thyself to sleep and leave thy vain bibble-babble.

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: Sir Topas!

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Maintain no words with him, good fellow. Who, I, sir? Not I, sir! God buy you, good Sir Topas. Marry, amen. I will, sir, I will.

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: Fool! Fool! Fool, I say!

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Alas, sir, be patient. What say you, sir? I am shent for speaking to you.

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: Good Fool, help me to some light and some paper. I tell thee, I am as well in my wits as any man in Illyria.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Welladay that you were, sir!

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: By this hand, I am. Good Fool, some ink, paper, and light; and convey what I will set down to my lady. It shall advantage thee more than ever the bearing of letter did.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: I will help you to ’t. But tell me true, are you not mad indeed, or do you but counterfeit?

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: Believe me, I am not. I tell thee true.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Nay, I’ll ne’er believe a madman till I see his brains. I will fetch you light and paper and ink.

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: Fool, I’ll requite it in the highest degree. I prithee, begone.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: I am gone, sir, and anon, sir, I’ll be with you again, In a trice, like to the old Vice, Your need to sustain. Who with dagger of lath, in his rage and his wrath, Cries “aha!” to the devil; Like a mad lad, “Pare thy nails, dad! Adieu, goodman devil.”

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
speeches.text: This is the air; that is the glorious sun. This pearl she gave me, I do feel ’t and see ’t. And though ’tis wonder that enwraps me thus, Yet ’tis not madness. Where’s Antonio, then? I could not find him at the Elephant. Yet there he was; and there I found this credit, That he did range the town to seek me out. His counsel now might do me golden service. For though my soul disputes well with my sense That this may be some error, but no madness, Yet doth this accident and flood of fortune So far exceed all instance, all discourse, That I am ready to distrust mine eyes And wrangle with my reason that persuades me To any other trust but that I am mad— Or else the lady’s mad. Yet if ’twere so, She could not sway her house, command her followers, Take and give back affairs and their dispatch With such a smooth, discreet, and stable bearing As I perceive she does. There’s something in ’t That is deceivable. But here the lady comes.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Blame not this haste of mine. If you mean well, Now go with me and with this holy man Into the chantry by. There, before him And underneath that consecrated roof, Plight me the full assurance of your faith, That my most jealous and too doubtful soul May live at peace. He shall conceal it Whiles you are willing it shall come to note, What time we will our celebration keep According to my birth. What do you say?

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
speeches.text: I’ll follow this good man and go with you, And, having sworn truth, ever will be true.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Then lead the way, good father, and heavens so shine That they may fairly note this act of mine.

speeches.speaker: FABIAN
speeches.text: Now, as thou lov’st me, let me see his letter.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Good Master Fabian, grant me another request.

speeches.speaker: FABIAN
speeches.text: Anything.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Do not desire to see this letter.

speeches.speaker: FABIAN
speeches.text: This is to give a dog and in recompense desire my dog again.

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: Belong you to the Lady Olivia, friends?

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Ay, sir, we are some of her trappings.

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: I know thee well. How dost thou, my good fellow?

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Truly, sir, the better for my foes and the worse for my friends.

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: Just the contrary: the better for thy friends.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: No, sir, the worse.

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: How can that be?

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Marry, sir, they praise me and make an ass of me. Now my foes tell me plainly I am an ass; so that by my foes, sir, I profit in the knowledge of myself, and by my friends I am abused. So that, conclusions to be as kisses, if your four negatives make your two affirmatives, why then the worse for my friends and the better for my foes.

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: Why, this is excellent.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: By my troth, sir, no—though it please you to be one of my friends.

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: Thou shalt not be the worse for me; there’s gold.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: But that it would be double-dealing, sir, I would you could make it another.

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: O, you give me ill counsel.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Put your grace in your pocket, sir, for this once, and let your flesh and blood obey it.

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: Well, I will be so much a sinner to be a double-dealer: there’s another.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Primo, secundo, tertio is a good play, and the old saying is, the third pays for all. The triplex, sir, is a good tripping measure, or the bells of Saint Bennet, sir, may put you in mind—one, two, three.

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: You can fool no more money out of me at this throw. If you will let your lady know I am here to speak with her, and bring her along with you, it may awake my bounty further.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Marry, sir, lullaby to your bounty till I come again. I go, sir, but I would not have you to think that my desire of having is the sin of covetousness. But, as you say, sir, let your bounty take a nap. I will awake it anon.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: Here comes the man, sir, that did rescue me.

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: That face of his I do remember well. Yet when I saw it last, it was besmeared As black as Vulcan in the smoke of war. A baubling vessel was he captain of, For shallow draught and bulk unprizable, With which such scatheful grapple did he make With the most noble bottom of our fleet That very envy and the tongue of loss Cried fame and honor on him.—What’s the matter?

speeches.speaker: FIRST OFFICER
speeches.text: Orsino, this is that Antonio That took the Phoenix and her fraught from Candy, And this is he that did the Tiger board When your young nephew Titus lost his leg. Here in the streets, desperate of shame and state, In private brabble did we apprehend him.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: He did me kindness, sir, drew on my side, But in conclusion put strange speech upon me. I know not what ’twas but distraction.

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: Notable pirate, thou saltwater thief, What foolish boldness brought thee to their mercies Whom thou, in terms so bloody and so dear, Hast made thine enemies?

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Orsino, noble sir, Be pleased that I shake off these names you give me. Antonio never yet was thief or pirate, Though, I confess, on base and ground enough, Orsino’s enemy. A witchcraft drew me hither. That most ingrateful boy there by your side From the rude sea’s enraged and foamy mouth Did I redeem; a wrack past hope he was. His life I gave him and did thereto add My love, without retention or restraint, All his in dedication. For his sake Did I expose myself, pure for his love, Into the danger of this adverse town; Drew to defend him when he was beset; Where, being apprehended, his false cunning (Not meaning to partake with me in danger) Taught him to face me out of his acquaintance And grew a twenty years’ removèd thing While one would wink; denied me mine own purse, Which I had recommended to his use Not half an hour before.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: How can this be?

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: When came he to this town?

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Today, my lord; and for three months before, No int’rim, not a minute’s vacancy, Both day and night did we keep company.

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: Here comes the Countess. Now heaven walks on Earth!— But for thee, fellow: fellow, thy words are madness. Three months this youth hath tended upon me— But more of that anon. Take him aside.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: What would my lord, but that he may not have, Wherein Olivia may seem serviceable?— Cesario, you do not keep promise with me.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: Madam?

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: Gracious Olivia—

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: What do you say, Cesario?—Good my lord—

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: My lord would speak; my duty hushes me.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: If it be aught to the old tune, my lord, It is as fat and fulsome to mine ear As howling after music.

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: Still so cruel?

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Still so constant, lord.

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: What, to perverseness? You, uncivil lady, To whose ingrate and unauspicious altars My soul the faithful’st off’rings have breathed out That e’er devotion tendered—what shall I do?

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Even what it please my lord that shall become him.

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: Why should I not, had I the heart to do it, Like to th’ Egyptian thief at point of death, Kill what I love?—a savage jealousy That sometime savors nobly. But hear me this: Since you to nonregardance cast my faith, And that I partly know the instrument That screws me from my true place in your favor, Live you the marble-breasted tyrant still. But this your minion, whom I know you love, And whom, by heaven I swear, I tender dearly, Him will I tear out of that cruel eye Where he sits crownèd in his master’s spite.— Come, boy, with me. My thoughts are ripe in mischief. I’ll sacrifice the lamb that I do love To spite a raven’s heart within a dove.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: And I, most jocund, apt, and willingly, To do you rest a thousand deaths would die.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Where goes Cesario?

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: After him I love More than I love these eyes, more than my life, More by all mores than e’er I shall love wife. If I do feign, you witnesses above, Punish my life for tainting of my love.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Ay me, detested! How am I beguiled!

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: Who does beguile you? Who does do you wrong?

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Hast thou forgot thyself? Is it so long?— Call forth the holy father.

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: Come, away!

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Whither, my lord?—Cesario, husband, stay.

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: Husband?

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Ay, husband. Can he that deny?

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: Her husband, sirrah?

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: No, my lord, not I.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Alas, it is the baseness of thy fear That makes thee strangle thy propriety. Fear not, Cesario. Take thy fortunes up. Be that thou know’st thou art, and then thou art As great as that thou fear’st. O, welcome, father. Father, I charge thee by thy reverence Here to unfold (though lately we intended To keep in darkness what occasion now Reveals before ’tis ripe) what thou dost know Hath newly passed between this youth and me.

speeches.speaker: PRIEST
speeches.text: A contract of eternal bond of love, Confirmed by mutual joinder of your hands, Attested by the holy close of lips, Strengthened by interchangement of your rings, And all the ceremony of this compact Sealed in my function, by my testimony; Since when, my watch hath told me, toward my grave I have traveled but two hours.

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: O thou dissembling cub! What wilt thou be When time hath sowed a grizzle on thy case? Or will not else thy craft so quickly grow That thine own trip shall be thine overthrow? Farewell, and take her, but direct thy feet Where thou and I henceforth may never meet.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: My lord, I do protest—

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: O, do not swear. Hold little faith, though thou hast too much fear.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: For the love of God, a surgeon! Send one presently to Sir Toby.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: What’s the matter?

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: Has broke my head across, and has given Sir Toby a bloody coxcomb too. For the love of God, your help! I had rather than forty pound I were at home.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Who has done this, Sir Andrew?

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: The Count’s gentleman, one Cesario. We took him for a coward, but he’s the very devil incardinate.

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: My gentleman Cesario?

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: ’Od’s lifelings, here he is!—You broke my head for nothing, and that that I did, I was set on to do ’t by Sir Toby.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: Why do you speak to me? I never hurt you. You drew your sword upon me without cause, But I bespake you fair and hurt you not.

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: If a bloody coxcomb be a hurt, you have hurt me. I think you set nothing by a bloody coxcomb. Here comes Sir Toby halting. You shall hear more. But if he had not been in drink, he would have tickled you othergates than he did.

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: How now, gentleman? How is ’t with you?

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: That’s all one. Has hurt me, and there’s th’ end on ’t. Sot, didst see Dick Surgeon, sot?

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: O, he’s drunk, Sir Toby, an hour agone; his eyes were set at eight i’ th’ morning.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Then he’s a rogue and a passy-measures pavin. I hate a drunken rogue.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Away with him! Who hath made this havoc with them?

speeches.speaker: ANDREW
speeches.text: I’ll help you, Sir Toby, because we’ll be dressed together.

speeches.speaker: TOBY
speeches.text: Will you help?—an ass-head, and a coxcomb, and a knave, a thin-faced knave, a gull?

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Get him to bed, and let his hurt be looked to.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
speeches.text: I am sorry, madam, I have hurt your kinsman, But, had it been the brother of my blood, I must have done no less with wit and safety. You throw a strange regard upon me, and by that I do perceive it hath offended you. Pardon me, sweet one, even for the vows We made each other but so late ago.

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: One face, one voice, one habit, and two persons! A natural perspective, that is and is not!

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
speeches.text: Antonio, O, my dear Antonio! How have the hours racked and tortured me Since I have lost thee!

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Sebastian are you?

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
speeches.text: Fear’st thou that, Antonio?

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: How have you made division of yourself? An apple cleft in two is not more twin Than these two creatures. Which is Sebastian?

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Most wonderful!

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
speeches.text: Do I stand there? I never had a brother, Nor can there be that deity in my nature Of here and everywhere. I had a sister Whom the blind waves and surges have devoured. Of charity, what kin are you to me? What countryman? What name? What parentage?

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: Of Messaline. Sebastian was my father. Such a Sebastian was my brother too. So went he suited to his watery tomb. If spirits can assume both form and suit, You come to fright us.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
speeches.text: A spirit I am indeed, But am in that dimension grossly clad Which from the womb I did participate. Were you a woman, as the rest goes even, I should my tears let fall upon your cheek And say “Thrice welcome, drownèd Viola.”

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: My father had a mole upon his brow.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
speeches.text: And so had mine.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: And died that day when Viola from her birth Had numbered thirteen years.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
speeches.text: O, that record is lively in my soul! He finishèd indeed his mortal act That day that made my sister thirteen years.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: If nothing lets to make us happy both But this my masculine usurped attire, Do not embrace me till each circumstance Of place, time, fortune, do cohere and jump That I am Viola; which to confirm, I’ll bring you to a captain in this town, Where lie my maiden weeds; by whose gentle help I was preserved to serve this noble count. All the occurrence of my fortune since Hath been between this lady and this lord.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
speeches.text: So comes it, lady, you have been mistook. But nature to her bias drew in that. You would have been contracted to a maid. Nor are you therein, by my life, deceived: You are betrothed both to a maid and man.

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: Be not amazed; right noble is his blood. If this be so, as yet the glass seems true, I shall have share in this most happy wrack.— Boy, thou hast said to me a thousand times Thou never shouldst love woman like to me.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: And all those sayings will I overswear, And all those swearings keep as true in soul As doth that orbèd continent the fire That severs day from night.

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: Give me thy hand, And let me see thee in thy woman’s weeds.

speeches.speaker: VIOLA
speeches.text: The Captain that did bring me first on shore Hath my maid’s garments. He, upon some action, Is now in durance at Malvolio’s suit, A gentleman and follower of my lady’s.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: He shall enlarge him. Fetch Malvolio hither. And yet, alas, now I remember me, They say, poor gentleman, he’s much distract. A most extracting frenzy of mine own From my remembrance clearly banished his. How does he, sirrah?

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Truly, madam, he holds Beelzebub at the stave’s end as well as a man in his case may do. Has here writ a letter to you. I should have given ’t you today morning. But as a madman’s epistles are no gospels, so it skills not much when they are delivered.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Open ’t and read it.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Look then to be well edified, when the Fool delivers the madman. By the Lord, madam—

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: How now, art thou mad?

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: No, madam, I do but read madness. An your Ladyship will have it as it ought to be, you must allow vox.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Prithee, read i’ thy right wits.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: So I do, madonna. But to read his right wits is to read thus. Therefore, perpend, my princess, and give ear.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Read it you, sirrah.

speeches.speaker: FABIAN
speeches.text: By the Lord, madam, you wrong me, and the world shall know it. Though you have put me into darkness and given your drunken cousin rule over me, yet have I the benefit of my senses as well as your Ladyship. I have your own letter that induced me to the semblance I put on, with the which I doubt not but to do myself much right or you much shame. Think of me as you please. I leave my duty a little unthought of and speak out of my injury. The madly used Malvolio.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Did he write this?

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Ay, madam.

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: This savors not much of distraction.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: See him delivered, Fabian. Bring him hither. My lord, so please you, these things further thought on, To think me as well a sister as a wife, One day shall crown th’ alliance on ’t, so please you, Here at my house, and at my proper cost.

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: Madam, I am most apt t’ embrace your offer. Your master quits you; and for your service done him, So much against the mettle of your sex, So far beneath your soft and tender breeding, And since you called me “master” for so long, Here is my hand. You shall from this time be Your master’s mistress.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: A sister! You are she.

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: Is this the madman?

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Ay, my lord, this same.— How now, Malvolio?

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: Madam, you have done me wrong, Notorious wrong.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Have I, Malvolio? No.

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: Lady, you have. Pray you peruse that letter. You must not now deny it is your hand. Write from it if you can, in hand or phrase, Or say ’tis not your seal, not your invention. You can say none of this. Well, grant it then, And tell me, in the modesty of honor, Why you have given me such clear lights of favor? Bade me come smiling and cross-gartered to you, To put on yellow stockings, and to frown Upon Sir Toby and the lighter people? And, acting this in an obedient hope, Why have you suffered me to be imprisoned, Kept in a dark house, visited by the priest, And made the most notorious geck and gull That e’er invention played on? Tell me why.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Alas, Malvolio, this is not my writing, Though I confess much like the character. But out of question, ’tis Maria’s hand. And now I do bethink me, it was she First told me thou wast mad; then cam’st in smiling, And in such forms which here were presupposed Upon thee in the letter. Prithee, be content. This practice hath most shrewdly passed upon thee. But when we know the grounds and authors of it, Thou shalt be both the plaintiff and the judge Of thine own cause.

speeches.speaker: FABIAN
speeches.text: Good madam, hear me speak, And let no quarrel nor no brawl to come Taint the condition of this present hour, Which I have wondered at. In hope it shall not, Most freely I confess, myself and Toby Set this device against Malvolio here, Upon some stubborn and uncourteous parts We had conceived against him. Maria writ The letter at Sir Toby’s great importance, In recompense whereof he hath married her. How with a sportful malice it was followed May rather pluck on laughter than revenge, If that the injuries be justly weighed That have on both sides passed.

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: Alas, poor fool, how have they baffled thee!

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: Why, “some are born great, some achieve greatness, and some have greatness thrown upon them.” I was one, sir, in this interlude, one Sir Topas, sir, but that’s all one. “By the Lord, Fool, I am not mad”—but, do you remember “Madam, why laugh you at such a barren rascal; an you smile not, he’s gagged”? And thus the whirligig of time brings in his revenges.

speeches.speaker: MALVOLIO
speeches.text: I’ll be revenged on the whole pack of you!

speeches.speaker: OLIVIA
speeches.text: He hath been most notoriously abused.

speeches.speaker: ORSINO
speeches.text: Pursue him and entreat him to a peace. He hath not told us of the Captain yet. When that is known, and golden time convents, A solemn combination shall be made Of our dear souls.—Meantime, sweet sister, We will not part from hence.—Cesario, come, For so you shall be while you are a man. But when in other habits you are seen, Orsino’s mistress, and his fancy’s queen.

speeches.speaker: FOOL
speeches.text: When that I was and a little tiny boy, With hey, ho, the wind and the rain, A foolish thing was but a toy, For the rain it raineth every day. But when I came to man’s estate, With hey, ho, the wind and the rain, ’Gainst knaves and thieves men shut their gate, For the rain it raineth every day. But when I came, alas, to wive, With hey, ho, the wind and the rain, By swaggering could I never thrive, For the rain it raineth every day. But when I came unto my beds, With hey, ho, the wind and the rain, With tosspots still had drunken heads, For the rain it raineth every day. A great while ago the world begun, With hey, ho, the wind and the rain, But that’s all one, our play is done, And we’ll strive to please you every day.
